thread:
incident-bot: SEV=2 pager triggered for service-discovery errors in us-west-az1. Symptoms: SRV lookups returning 5xx / NXDOMAIN intermittently across multiple clusters. Impact: internal control-plane API calls and a subset of customer Dedicated endpoints failing. Pager: https://incidents.redwood/2234567800 :rotating_light:

elaine (oncall): acked. I'm on the incident. Linking runbook: /runbooks/consul-srv-lookup. Collecting initial scope. Who's on netops? @maria-netops can you check inter-AZ peering?

ryan-sre: I see coreDNS upstreams returning connection resets to consul-proxy. grep from coredns logs:

```
2026-03-14T21:10:07Z coredns[proxy]: upstream consul://10.10.5.12:8600: dial tcp 10.10.5.12:8600: connect: connection reset by peer
2026-03-14T21:10:08Z coredns[proxy]: failed to query SRV _internal._tcp.example.svc.cluster.local: 502
consul: raft: peer 10.10.5.12:8300 rejected heartbeat: snapshot-in-progress
```

ryan-sre: Looks like consul leader is churning and at least one server is in snapshot/restore state. Multiple nodes briefly unreachable over TCP 8300/8301.

maria-netops: Confirmed BGP session churn between us-west-az1 and us-west-az2 starting ~21:08 UTC, causing occasional TCP resets across the peering fabric. We've got partial egress if packets return via az3, but flows to some consul nodes in az2 are dropping. Investigating switching traffic via az3 to stabilize.

dmitri-eng: Pushing a quick mitigation: lowering CoreDNS TTL and enabling local fallback to cached SRV entries to reduce immediate pressure on consul. Patch applied to kube-system/coredns configmap:

```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns --type merge -p '{"data":{"Corefile":".:53 {\n    errors\n    log\n    cache 30\n    forward . /etc/resolv.conf\n}\n"}}'
```

This will reduce cache lifetime and let pods use cached entries when consul is briefly unreachable. Rolling restart coredns pods now.

support-swift: Customer impact summary for public comms: 12 Dedicated customers reported elevated 503s for background sync jobs (internal calls to control plane). Internal on-call reports from 3 product teams. No external hosted API outages reported. Messaging draft: "We're investigating internal service discovery errors in us-west; some background jobs may be delayed." Thoughts?

elaine (oncall): That messaging looks fine. Set cadence to 15m updates. @ryan-sre, can you confirm consul cluster health and leader state?

ryan-sre: Running consul operator health checks now. Output:

```
$ consul operator raft list-peers
Node            ID                                     Address         State
consul-0        e8a...                                 10.10.5.10:8300  leader
consul-1        b1c...                                 10.10.6.11:8300  follower
consul-2        9f2...                                 10.10.7.12:8300  follower (snapshotting)
```

ryan-sre: consul-2 is in snapshotting/restore state and not responding to heartbeat probes reliably. I don't want an immediate forced-evict unless we have to.

maria-netops: We started a steering change at 21:25 UTC to prefer us-west-az3 paths for TCP to ports 8300-8302 and 8500 (consul RPC/serf). CLI we used: cloudctl routes update --prefix 10.10.5.0/24 --next-hop az3-gw --filter tcp:8300-8500

maria-netops: After route change, packet loss to consul-2 dropped from 18% -> 1% in metrics.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation in progress — traffic steered to us-west-az3 for consul ports.

dmitri-eng: After steering, coredns error rate dropped ~70% and service discovery 5xx rate decreased. Rolling restarts completed. Monitoring for resumed leader elections.

ryan-sre: After mitigation, consul cluster shows stable leader, raft metrics returned to normal. Still seeing occasional slow RPCs from consul-2 while it finishes snapshot apply. Keeping it in the cluster for now.

support-swift: Updated customer note: "Mitigation applied; internal service discovery is improving. Some background jobs may be delayed. We will follow up when fully resolved." Posted to status page.

elaine (oncall): Good. Prepare handoff: I'm handing to @oncall-rotation in 30m. Leaving notes:
- Root cause: inter-AZ peering churn -> TCP resets to consul ports -> consul node snapshot/restore + leader churn -> CoreDNS upstream errors and SRV lookup failures.
- Mitigation: netops steering via az3 for consul ports, coredns TTL lowered and pods restarted to reduce immediate lookup load, monitoring for consul snapshot completion.
- Next steps: consider replacing consul-2 if it doesn't finish snapshot in 2h (evict + bootstrap from snapshot), coordinate a safe window for forced-remove if needed.

ryan-sre: Adding a quick check list for next oncall:
1) consul operator raft list-peers (confirm leader stable)
2) consul members and operator snapshot inspect for errors
3) coredns 5xx rate and forward errors
4) netops BGP adjacency metrics for us-west-az1/az2
\dmitri-eng: I'll follow up with a durable config change to add a local stub resolver in node bootstrap to reduce cross-AZ lookups long term. Filing a follow-up RFC/PR.

oncall-rotation: ACK will take primary in 30m. Please @mention me if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV=3 (mitigated) at 2234569000. Next update scheduled in 30m. :white_check_mark:

elaine (oncall): handoff complete at 2234569222, leaving monitoring alerts in place and assigning followups: #followup-consul-az-peering. Thanks team.
